id: security-audit
name: Structured security audit
blocks:
  - id: orient
    use: flyt-blocks-inquiry:orient
    title: Survey repository structure
    config:
      effort: medium
      maxSteps: 30
      instructions: "Locate the repository under the repos/ directory in the workspace. Map its layout: languages, frameworks, entry points, dependency manifests, config files, and trust boundaries. Summarize the attack surface and which areas warrant the deepest review. Do not modify anything."
  - id: plan
    use: flyt-blocks-core:plan-start
    title: Plan audit areas
    config:
      effort: medium
      instructions: "Using the orientation, produce well-defined audit tasks covering the identified attack surface (e.g. input handling, auth/session, dependency vulnerabilities, secrets, file handling, network calls, deserialization).   - id: review
    use: flyt-blocks-core:work
    title: Investigate and write finding reports
    config:
      effort: high
      maxSteps: 200
      effect: workspace-change

    title: Verify report completeness
    config:
      effort: medium
      instructions: "Read findings/summary.md and the individual finding reports. Verify each report explains the vulnerability, cites affected files, states a severity matching its filename prefix, and includes reproducible verification steps. Verify summary.md has a 'Confirmed findings' section listing every report. If anything is missing or inconsistent, fix the reports directly and return the final state."

proposals.rationale: Restructures the loop into a staged security review: orient on the repo, plan audit areas, execute the review writing one Markdown report per confirmed vulnerability into findings/, then verify consistency and produce a summary index. Enables the file tools the loop needs and adds mechanical acceptance checks. No audit is executed now; this only authors the loop.

diff.after: Structured security audit of cloned repository

Perform an authorized, read-only security review of the locally cloned repository under the workspace's repos directory. Investigate step by step: enumerate the codebase and dependencies, identify candidate vulnerabilities (injection, auth flaws, unsafe deserialization, secrets, SSRF, path traversal, etc.), confirm each with concrete code evidence, and write one Markdown report per confirmed vulnerability into a findings/ folder. Each report must explain the vulnerability, affected files/lines, severity (low, medium, or high), impact, and reproducible verification steps (commands or manual walkthrough). Filenames must be prefixed with the severity, e.g. findings/high-sql-injection-login.md. Also maintain findings/summary.md listing all confirmed findings. Do not exploit, modify, or exfiltrate anything; the repo is authorized for local review only.

Analysis only: never execute exploit payloads against live services, never modify the audited repository, never exfiltrate data. Only report confirmed vulnerabilities backed by specific code evidence; discard speculative ones. All reports go in findings/ with severity-prefixed filenames.
